items.title: Cabrini ED care wraps 24 minutes earlier using AI scribe
items.summary: A Melbourne emergency department measured what an AI scribe actually saved, rather than asking how it felt.

_homepage.note: The Cabrini pilot ran across more than 1,600 encounters in four weeks, saved an average of 31 minutes on note entry, finished episodes of care 24 minutes earlier, and left 97 per cent of the clinicians wanting to keep it — enough for a twelve-month extension into the ED short stay unit. The caveat is the useful part: there is no EMR integration, so clinicians paste reviewed notes into a free-text field, and the ED director has tied any renewal beyond the year to a demonstrated return on investment. It is the nearest thing to real Australian ED numbers on these tools instead of a vendor claim.

items.title: Have You Ever Heard Old Music? 52 Essential Records
items.summary: Out today: the Old Music Friday producer's fifty-two records, written out at length for the first time.

_homepage.note: This is Owen Cutts, the man behind Old Music Friday — the record writing this feed has been trying to find a live URL for since his own site stopped resolving. The fifty-two run through Minnie Riperton, The Delfonics, Al Green and Dusty Springfield, and include both The Beatles and Aretha Franklin, who are already on the shelves at home. Published 5 November; the listings disagree on ISBN, with most shops using 9781399644808 and Hachette's own page carrying a second one.

items.title: US Probe: POCUS for the Shoulder
items.summary: Confirming a shoulder reduction with the probe instead of sending the patient back for a second film.

_homepage.note: Post-reduction confirmation and rotator cuff assessment are the two shoulder applications that return real time to a department, and both are learnable in an afternoon with a linear probe you already pick up for lines and lungs. It sits just outside the formal CCPU core but uses the same habits, and it is the scan that stops a trolley sitting in the corridor waiting on radiology. The case-led format makes the landmarks stick better than a textbook chapter.

items.title: The key policies on offer in the 2026 Victorian election
items.summary: Every party's health commitment on one page, three weeks before he votes on them.

_homepage.note: Polling day is 28 November, and the promises collected here are the ones that land on a roster: Labor's pledge to expand a dozen emergency departments by 25 per cent and hire 1,500 more health workers, the Coalition's surgery wait-time and patient transit lounge plans, the Greens' push to standardise electronic medical records statewide. The feed has carried these announcements one at a time as they were made; this is the page that finally holds them side by side. Most of them still have no delivery timeline attached, which is itself the detail worth noticing.

items.title: POCUS in the ED: Is Confirmatory RUQ US Still Necessary?
items.summary: The argument for backing your own biliary scan when the surgical team asks for a formal one.

_homepage.note: The trial behind this gave surgeons the history, the bloods and the bedside scan, then asked whether adding a formal radiology RUQ changed their plan at all — which is the question that decides whether a patient waits four more hours or goes home. Biliary is core CCPU territory, and the 89.8% sensitivity and 88.0% specificity quoted here for cholelithiasis is the number to have ready when the registrar on the other end of the phone wants the formal study. The post is honest that none of it transfers to an operator who isn't confident with the probe yet.

items.title: GTA VI pre-load starts November 10 with a 212 GB file
items.summary: The date to start the download, nine days before launch, on a file big enough to need planning first.

_homepage.note: Pre-load opens at 12:00am local time on 10 November, nine days ahead of the 19 November launch, and Rockstar's 212 GB is required free space rather than the download size — so the real job is deciding what comes off the PS5 drive, and that is a weekend task, not a launch-night one. The feed already carried the file size confirmation; this is the date that makes it actionable. Physical code-in-box copies run on a separate 12 November schedule.

items.title: Inside Mutimer's First Physical Store
items.summary: Six years selling only online, then a Smith Street shop — and the brand's reasoning is the interesting part.

_homepage.note: Mutimer is one of the two modern Australian labels this brief watches by name, and this is the piece on the Smith Street space that ended six years of direct-to-consumer only. The argument for it came from their own numbers: the pop-ups converted better in person than the website ever did, which is a physical store justified with data rather than romance. Collingwood, so it is a walk from the places the feed keeps sending him to eat.

items.title: World's Best Tattoo Artists for 2026, With Seven Australians
items.summary: Five of the seven Australians on this year's list work out of Melbourne studios.

_homepage.note: Kris Sunkee at Compendium works across black-and-grey realism and blackwork, and Jake Danielson at Umbra is one of this year's new entrants — two bookable names in the city rather than another directory page of SEO filler, which is what almost every Melbourne tattoo search returns. The underlying GRAPHICA ranking is a popularity exercise, so treat it as a shortlist for going and looking at portfolios instead of a verdict. It is the first genuinely Australian-weighted tattoo item this feed has had.

items.title: TBS 2026: Best Intensive Care Medicine Papers
items.summary: A year of critical care literature compressed to the papers that actually changed what people do.

_homepage.note: The Big Sick round-ups are the one annual list worth reading end to end, because the St Emlyn's team selects on whether a paper changes a Tuesday night shift rather than on how often it gets cited. Previous editions carried DanGer Shock, the serratus plane block work for rib fractures and the double sequential defibrillation timing question — all of which landed in Australian departments within months. Read it as a reading list to work through, not as a substitute for the papers.

items.title: Your photo of the year 2026 (and my photo of the year 2026)
items.summary: The annual open call to submit one frame and say why it is the one; submissions are running now.

_homepage.note: This thread is where the site's best writing comes from every year — one picture, a few hundred words on why it mattered, and none of the gear-review scaffolding that fills the rest of the archive. Entries are already going up, so the shape of what gets accepted is visible before you write anything. A year of rolls is a year of candidates, and this is an unusually low-friction way to put a frame in front of people who actually shoot film.

items.title: Subtle Black and White with a Contax RTS II and Rollei Retro 80s
items.summary: What Rollei Retro 80s does to skin and foliage, shown in frames rather than described in a spec sheet.

_homepage.note: Retro 80s sits at the near-infrared end of the black-and-white range, and the glow it puts on faces is the kind of thing you want to see in somebody else's pictures before you commit a roll and a developing run to it. Ibraar Hussain shoots it on a Contax RTS II with adapted M42 glass, which is the cheap end of genuinely good lenses and a sensible match for a film this particular. Files neatly next to the Konica infrared second attempt the feed carried in October.

items.title: Ten to Try: Brunswick's Best New Restaurants and Bakeries
items.summary: A suburb-level list instead of a city-wide one, which is the only sort you can actually walk to.

_homepage.note: Brunswick and Brunswick East in a single piece: a Greek restaurant, three scroll shops, and Vandels on Nicholson Street run by a former Beatrix baker. Patris and Stefanino Panino have already come through this feed on their own; the value here is the places that never got a First Look of their own. Published early September, which means everything on it has had two months to settle into whether it is good or merely new.
